clue.text: Jumping fault is problem for horse

indicators.note: jumping letters leap about out of their order, so fault is gets rearranged

explanation.surface: A showjumping commentator blames a refusal on some ailment troubling the horse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jumping' sounds like the horse's event but signals the anagram of FAULT IS.
explanation.definitionFit: A fistula is an abnormal channel or ulcer; horses suffer it notably at the withers or poll, so it is a classic equine ailment.

clue.text: Fry, perhaps, cutting his border plant

indicators.note: cutting means the performer's word is inserted, splitting the outline letters

parts.note: his refers back to Fry, whose border letters are F and Y
Stephen Fry is an example of an actor

explanation.surface: Stephen Fry trimming the edging of his garden plants.
explanation.walkthrough: Stephen Fry is a British actor and comedian.
explanation.definitionFit: A plant in the industrial sense is a works or manufacturing site, such as a mill.

clue.text: Staggered if Google's singing Do- Re-Mi

indicators.note: staggered means the letters of if Google's lurch into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone is astonished that Google's search engine can sing the scale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Staggered' looks like amazed but signals the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: Solfeggio is the method of vocal exercise using sol-fa syllables to name scale notes.

clue.text: Built up city outlaw

parts.note: Ur was an ancient Sumerian city
to outlaw something is to ban it

explanation.surface: A fugitive has grown into a powerful figure in the town.
explanation.definitionFit: A built-up area is a town or city district densely covered by buildings.

clue.text: Bark of rabbit ingesting soft drugs regularly

indicators.note: ingesting means the rabbit swallows the chosen letters

parts.note: an Angora is a long-haired breed of rabbit

indicators.note: regularly here means every third letter of soft drugs is taken

explanation.surface: A rabbit regularly nibbles on soft drugs, eating them along with bark.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes every third letter of SOFT DRUGS, giving STU.
explanation.definitionFit: Angostura is the aromatic bitter bark of a South American tree, used for tonics and bitters.

clue.text: Story of girl on fire turned into unbalanced article

indicators.note: into means one piece is put inside another, here the burning word goes into the crazy one

parts.note: unbalanced in mind means mad

indicators.note: turned means the word for burning is read backwards

parts.note: on fire means lit
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A tale about a girl whose burning anger turned her into something deranged.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unbalanced article' looks like one idea but splits into two pieces: the crazed word, then the indefinite article.
explanation.definitionFit: Roald Dahl's novel about a brilliant young girl with telekinetic powers is titled with her name, so the book is literally a girl's story.

clue.text: See 17
Prepare top of dam to retain water for main source of power

indicators.note: retain means the outer word holds the moisture word inside it

parts.note: to prepare is to train
dew is water condensed on surfaces

indicators.note: top of means the first letter of dam

explanation.surface: Engineers get a dam ready to hold water back for hydroelectric power.
explanation.walkthrough: The main is the open sea; trade winds drove sailing ships.
explanation.definitionFit: Trade winds are steady ocean winds that powered merchant sailing ships across the sea.

clue.text: Fruit producers' pride slightly dented

indicators.note: slightly dented means the word is knocked a little out of shape, one letter shifted

parts.note: a pride is a group of lions

explanation.surface: An orchard grower's self-esteem has taken a small knock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'slightly dented' shifts the O of LIONS one place earlier.
explanation.definitionFit: The Bible speaks of the fruit of one's loins, meaning children, so those body parts produce fruit.

clue.text: Having spaces between planes spare

definitions.meaning: having angles, the space between two intersecting planes
spare means lean and bony in build

explanation.surface: An aviation note about gaps between aircraft that are not in use.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both having sharp angles and, of a person, thin and bony.

clue.text: Once Lebanon featured small star

indicators.note: featured means the letters appear within the words Once Lebanon

explanation.surface: A tiny celebrity once appeared in a Lebanese production.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is a clipped, short form of celebrity, a famous person or star, hence a small version of the word for a star.

clue.text: Laughter at bunk where some prisoners sleep

parts.note: bunk means nonsense, or guff
prisons are divided into wings lettered A, B and so on, and A wing is one of them

explanation.surface: Mocking laughter aimed at a prison cell bunk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bunk' looks like a bed, which fits the prison scene, but it means nonsense; 'at' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Guffawing is loud, hearty laughter, a gerund used as a noun for the act of laughing heartily.

definitions.meaning: seven is the sum of the two numbers one plus six
one shilling and sixpence in old money was eighteen pence, worth seven and a half new pence after decimalisation

explanation.surface: A bare pair of figures that looks like a sum or a price list entry.
explanation.walkthrough: Before 1971 British money had shillings (12 old pence) and a shilling was worth 5 new pence.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase works both as arithmetic, a unit and a half dozen totalling seven, and as the pre-decimal price of eighteen old pence.

clue.text: Stand to rest Labour leader

parts.note: to rest is to ease off

indicators.note: leader means the first letter of the word Labour

explanation.surface: A call for the head of the Labour Party to stand down and take a rest.
explanation.definitionFit: An easel is a frame or stand that holds a painting or board upright.

clue.text: Meditative about following bear

indicators.note: following means the short word for about comes after the bear

parts.note: Yogi Bear is the cartoon bear
c, short for circa, means about

explanation.surface: A meditative mood descends while trailing behind a bear.
explanation.definitionFit: Yogic describes the practice of yoga, which centres on meditation and contemplation.

clue.text: Sort out 1 across before finishing bran and toast for breakfast, perhaps

indicators.note: sort out means the gathered letters are put into a new order

parts.note: the numeral one looks like I

indicators.note: finishing means the last letters of bran and toast

explanation.surface: Choosing between bran and toast for breakfast after dealing with a clue.
explanation.walkthrough: '1 across' looks like a grid reference, but gives I and ACROSS as written.
explanation.definitionFit: A croissant is a flaky pastry roll typically eaten in the morning meal, an example of it.

clue.text: Found pair surprisingly not yet purchased

indicators.note: surprisingly means the letters of Found pair turn up in an unexpected order

explanation.surface: Someone was startled to discover a pair of shoes nobody had bought.
explanation.definitionFit: Goods unpaid for have not been bought yet, since nobody has handed over money for them.

clue.text: Dominant reverend father's around after Ash Wednsday

indicators.note: around means the parent word surrounds the clergy title

parts.note: pa is a familiar word for father
Lent is the season that begins on Ash Wednesday

explanation.surface: A senior clergyman's father appears in church after Ash Wednesday.
explanation.definitionFit: Prevalent means widespread or predominant, prevailing over others.

clue.text: Drinks fit criminal from unknown story of animal cunning

parts.note: Fantas are cans of the fizzy drink Fanta
a fit is a spasm or tic

indicators.note: criminal suggests something crooked, so from is twisted around

parts.note: x is the unknown in algebra

explanation.surface: Accused crook fits the profile, drinking at a mystery venue.
explanation.definitionFit: Roald Dahl's tale of a wily fox who outwits three farmers is a story about an animal's cunning.

clue.text: Sweet cold drink in sweltering mid-September

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold on taps

indicators.note: in means the drink goes inside the word for sweltering

parts.note: sweltering means hot
cola is a soft drink

indicators.note: mid means the middle letter of September is taken

explanation.surface: A sweet, chilled drink on a sweltering day in the middle of September.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sweet' could be an adjective for the drink but is a noun, a confection.
explanation.definitionFit: A chocolate is a sweet, a small confection, in the British sense of sweet as a piece of candy.

clue.text: Angel's chief character on radio

definitions.meaning: in the TV series ... Angels, the unseen boss of the detectives
the radio alphabet word for C

explanation.surface: The head of a heavenly being becomes a voice on the airwaves.
explanation.definitionFit: The name is both the employer in Charlie's Angels and the NATO phonetic code word for C.

clue.text: Champion of the world and windy city

indicators.note: windy means twisting like a winding road, so and is rearranged

parts.note: NY is New York city

explanation.surface: A boast that Chicago, the windy city, holds the world title.
explanation.walkthrough: 'windy city' suggests Chicago, but 'windy' twists AND and the city is NY.
explanation.definitionFit: Roald Dahl's novel Danny the Champion of the World is named after its boy hero, who earns that title.

clue.text: Slightly jaundiced old solvers extremely likely to maintain depression

parts.note: ye is an old form of you, the solvers

indicators.note: to maintain means the outer letters hold the hollow inside them
extremely means the outer letters of likely

parts.note: a low is a depression in weather or mood

explanation.surface: Older crossword solvers are likely to be a little jaded and gloomy.
explanation.definitionFit: Jaundice turns skin yellow, so slightly jaundiced skin has a tinge of that colour.

clue.text: Deep in baby's subconscious

indicators.note: in means the letters lie inside the words baby's subconscious

explanation.surface: Something deep buried in an infant's unconscious mind.
explanation.definitionFit: The deep is a poetic noun for the sea's depths or a bottomless gulf, matching a chasm or bottomless pit.

clue.text: Coordinate German eight in boat

parts.note: y is the coordinate on the vertical axis
acht is German for eight

explanation.surface: Organising a German rowing eight inside a boat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'eight' suggests a rowing crew, fitting 'boat', but just gives the German word.
explanation.definitionFit: A yacht is a sailing or motor vessel used for racing or pleasure, a kind of boat.

clue.text: Author had a droll style

indicators.note: style here means the letters of had a droll are restyled into a new order

explanation.surface: A writer who possessed a wry, witty manner of writing.
explanation.definitionFit: The writer of Matilda, The BFG and many children's stories, famous for his darkly comic tone.

clue.text: Lift from Sierra is exciting

indicators.note: from means the letters are taken out of the run Sierra is exciting

explanation.surface: Taking a ride up a mountain range is thrilling.
explanation.definitionFit: To lift something is to elevate it or move it higher, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Shop said to be in Indian district

indicators.note: said means the word for the shop is spoken, and a sound-alike is written

parts.note: a deli is a delicatessen shop

explanation.surface: A shop reportedly located in some region of India.
explanation.definitionFit: Delhi is the Indian capital territory, an administrative region containing New Delhi.

clue.text: Developing vital cure is profitable

indicators.note: developing means the letters of vital cure are worked into something new

explanation.surface: A drug company finds that a life-saving treatment brings in money.
explanation.definitionFit: Lucrative means producing much money, a direct synonym of profitable.

clue.text: John keeps dry in game

indicators.note: keeps means the toilet holds the abstainer's letters inside it

parts.note: john is slang for a toilet, a loo
dry means teetotal, abbreviated TT

explanation.surface: A man called John stays sober during a game.
explanation.walkthrough: John is an American and British slang word for the lavatory.
explanation.definitionFit: Lotto is a game of chance, a lottery or a form of bingo with numbered cards.

clue.text: Give right measure of print to Herald, say

parts.note: an en is a printer's unit of width
the Herald is an example of a newspaper title

explanation.surface: Granting a newspaper the right to publish a certain amount of print.
explanation.definitionFit: To entitle someone is to give them a claim or a right to something.

clue.text: Nervous that we're starting to be irritating

indicators.note: starting means the opening letters of the words that and we're

parts.note: an irritating rash feels itchy

explanation.surface: Someone frets that the solvers are getting annoyed.
explanation.definitionFit: Twitchy describes someone jumpy and on edge, a colloquial synonym of nervous.
